General Site Presence
in Live MHU
Patients accessing tools, materials or unsecured areas

General Site Presence
in Live MHU
Battery tools preferred; work only during agreed hours; noise monitoring (≤80 dB); toolbox talks on minimising noise; clinical team briefed on schedule.
Unlocked door during replacement allowing patient access to tools
One door replaced per day; room locked immediately after new door fitted; tools removed/secured before leaving room; clinical induction + daily checklist.
New door monitors (KG500) creating unintended ligature points if not sealed
KG500 fitted and tested as part of Kingsway complete system; anti-pick sealant applied; Warringtonfire FoA compliance confirmed.
Open window opening allowing escape or ligature attempt

Windows removed and sealed externally; temporary anti-ligature blanking panel fitted immediately; no internal reveal work required after external sealing; ceiling void wiring done from loft (no room entry needed).
Polar + MPMH (Lee Gemell and A. sanson)
Contractors leaving window unsecured while working
External sealing protocol strictly followed; daily checklist confirms opening secured; no work left overnight with open aperture.
Dust from vinyl removal and IPS panel removal contaminating air
HAI-SCRIBE controls (Class II/III); on-tool extraction + FFP3 masks; water suppression instead of dry sweeping; daily deep clean of work area.
Manual handling of heavy debris (old flooring, IPS panels)
Mechanical aids and team lifting; manual handling toolbox talk; reduce load sizes.
Altro Whiterock cladding and Altro Aquarius flooring creating slip/trip hazards during installation
Housekeeping maintained; non-slip flooring installed progressively; barriers and signage around wet works.
Tools or materials left in room creating ligature or weapon risk
Daily tool checklist (sign in/out); tools removed at end of every shift; secure tool bags/lockable chests; no overnight storage in rooms.
Accountability updated to NHS primary per patient risk assessment review (Apr 2026)
Falls from steps or hop-ups during cladding/IPS installation
Stepladder permit required daily; PASMA-trained operatives; no work below others.
Electric shock or gas leak during service isolation
Services isolated by authorised persons (Robert Smith / Stephen Donovan); confirmation drawings used; lock-out/tag-out procedures.
Waste left in room or corridor creating trip or ligature hazard
Lockable/lidded skips used; waste removed daily; no accumulation allowed.
Patient attempts to enter work area or shows distress
Stop work immediately; secure area and alert nursing staff; never manage patient behaviour yourself.
Accountability updated to NHS primary per patient risk assessment review (Apr 2026)
Cumulative disruption to patients over project duration
Maximum 3 rooms worked at a time; weekly ward briefings; clear communication of schedule to ward team.
Accountability updated to NHS primary per patient risk assessment review (Apr 2026)
